 Atletico Madrid return to LaLiga action at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano in Madrid, hosting Deportivo de A Coruna in what represents a significant home test for Diego Simeone's side. 
 Atletico arrive at this fixture in strong domestic form, sitting second in LaLiga and having strung together a run of results that marks them out as genuine title contenders. Their 2-1 win over Real Madrid in September and a 2-0 Champions League victory over Manchester United underline the quality Simeone has at his disposal this season. 
 The midweek trip to Germany provided a reality check of sorts. Atletico drew 1-1 with VfB Stuttgart in the Champions League, coming from behind and finishing the match with ten men, though Julian Alvarez's goal to level the tie was a moment of genuine quality from the Argentine forward. 
 Deportivo arrive in Madrid sitting ninth in LaLiga, a position that flatters neither their ambitions nor their recent form. Antonio Hidalgo's side have won just one of their last five competitive matches and head into this fixture with a lengthy injury list that will test the depth of his squad. 
 Atletico have dominated the head-to-head record in recent years, and Deportivo's travel record this season gives Simeone's side further reason for confidence. The Riyadh Air Metropolitano has been a fortress, and Atletico will look to make that count here.
